pr_body:
pkg/cloud: Expand Azure backups functionality

Add KMS support for Azure KeyVaults. This lets users encrypt and decrypt backups using keys stored in Azure KeyVault. It is used in a similar way as KMS support is currently for GCP and AWS, that is, by running a CRDB backup or restore command with options `with kms='azure:///key/version?PARAM1=value&PARAM2=value...'` The required params are:

```
AZURE_TENANT_ID
AZURE_CLIENT_ID
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
AZURE_VAULT_NAME
```

Add App Registration authentication for Azure Storage and Azure KeyVault support. This new authentication method is also called Azure RBAC (Role-Based Authentication Control). It is an Azure-wide authentication system. Previously we had only supported "storage keys," a legacy authentication mechanism that applies only to Storage. Since we need RBAC for KeyVault, we add support for it to Storage for consistency. RBAC authentication is configured with three of the four above URI parameters (Tenant ID, Client ID, and Client Secret).

To use RBAC with KMS, the following Azure permissions must be granted to the authenticating role:
```
"dataActions": [
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/encrypt/action",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/decrypt/action"
],
```

To use RBAC with Storage, the built-in Azure role `Storage Blob Data Contributor` can be granted.


Note that an upcoming PR, https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/96825, will add Implicit Authentication to both of these services; more details are available in that PRs description.

Note that ASSUME ROLE is not offered here, as Azure does not support it at this time. It will be available "soon."

Release note (enterprise change): Add KMS support for Azure KeyVaults. Add App Registration authentication for Azure Storage and Azure KeyVault support.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/86903
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/96459)
also, i'd be happy to eagerly merge the new vendor packages in a seperate PR, to avoid constant rebasing and `./dev gen`'ing in this more involved PR.

Thanks for doing this! I'm still to review the PR but leaving some high level nits: 
- the title line of the commit message should be prefixed with the package that has been affected. We also strive to keep the title shorter than 50 characters as specified in https://wiki.crdb.io/wiki/spaces/CRDB/pages/73072807/Git+Commit+Messages#Commit-title.

- can I ask you to expand on the commit message? A few things that come to mind are describing what "App Registration" is, what new parameters an Azure URI accepts and what they represent, and an example of a KMS URI.

> though I'm unsure why this needs to be in a roachtest  

In the past, we did not have the Cloud Unit Test job in CI and so had to exclusively  rely on roachtests to test the KMS logic. If we want to port those over to integration tests that run as part of the job we could, but I don't know whether it is worth the effort 🤷

> this looks great thus far and thanks for wrangling azure! I think we need a bit more testing. Some places to add to:
> 
> 1. Could you add a `azure_kms_test.go` that tests some of the specific azure_kms shenanigans, similar to `aws_kms_test.go`? Happy to walk you through how to add env vars to TC build agents.

🤦 I did, just didn't add it to the commit, which is _also_ why the test build failed.

> 2. We ought to verify that this works in the wild with backup/restore as well. we currently do this for other kms services in `pkg/cmd/roachtest/tests/backup.go`, though I'm unsure why this needs to be in a roachtest. @adityamaru do you know why?

Yup, I tested manually, and will arrange to add the fixtures to the nightly job shortly
Oh, I missed your reference to ` pkg/cmd/roachtest/tests/backup.go` - I'll add a test there too! ...Not much interest from me in porting that anywhere right now, though :)
Tests are all green, ready for another look!
awesome work! just left some non-blocking stuff.

Does this get us Azure KMS for changefeeds as well as DR stuff? cc @HonoreDB 

If not, we should open an issue @amruss.

@benbardin I realized after reviewing the implicit auth PR that the the release note in this PR could use a bit more details. Specifically, I think docs folks would appreciate some directions on how to use this feature, i.e. what are the new syntax and semantics for azure kms?
Expanded the PR description a bit as per our discussion in Slack!

issue_context.title: backupccl: support encrypted backups with Azure Key Vault (KMS)
issue_context.body:
Add support for [Azure Key Vault](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/key-vault/) (KMS) alongside our current support for AWS and GCP KMS.

Jira issue: CRDB-18997

Epic CRDB-18954

review_comments: the commit message contains some language around "App registration authentication". what's the deal there? Ctrl+f of "registration" in this commit didn't point me to anything.
Added a comment to azure_storage.go, where the constants live.
non blocking: mind adding a comment that says: "passing startIndex=i will start the fmt strings at $i+1". I found this new arg a bit hard to follow.
done
could you add a comment that explains why this algo was chosen?
done
Sounds good.

either in this PR, or in a follow up, we ought move the first 20 or so lines here that are not specific to Azure to general KMS URI parser helper func. It seems the same logic here is applied to google and aws, and who likes repeat code?
+1, but I do vote follow-up :)
can kms run using the `azure_account_key` auth method? If so, perhaps it's worth adding a test variant for this flavor of auth as well.

No, that doesn't work, "account key" is only for azure storage. Turns out every Azure service has it's own localized authentication mechanism that doesn't work anywhere else. Sometimes it even breaks the standardized auth mechanism!
oh man, this is so much cleaner than running the test using a roachtest. thanks for doing this!!
you're welcome!
it's a bit sad that there's all this manual url wrangling, unlike our other kms implementations. Is this a product of azure being naughty?
Yeah, basically. The Azure Keyvault API takes in a URL (maybe most of their APIs do). Other SDKs remember their own endpoints and regions. 🤷

could you add one more sentences on the implication of this param? I.e. if the client specifies this, they have a "secret" credential, as oppose to a "shared" credential? I'm not entirely sure what the implications are here.
Yeah, I'll add a big comment. I think App Registration is a term of art that will be familiar to Azure users, but you're right that it is _not_ clear to CRDB devs, so I'll elaborate here. Thanks!

great comment. thanks! A just to be clear, the 2nd option requires "AZURE_CLIENT_ID", "AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET" and "AZURE_TENANT_ID", while the third option just requires "AZURE_ACCOUNT_KEY", right? Could you specific this in the comment?
Yeah - I revised the comment and made that super-explicit, thanks!
at least this part of the azure kms  interface looks clean :)
Yes!
